comment: The single-cell A-pose reference guide -- the T-pose's sibling, in the same normalised cell space (x and y run 0..1 across one cell, y down). Each arm is the T-pose's arm rotated 45 degrees down about its own shoulder, segment lengths preserved, so the two guides describe the same figure in two poses rather than two figures. Everything else -- head, neck, hip, knees, feet at y 0.92 -- is identical to tpose_female.json on purpose: a character drawn from either guide has to reconstruct to the same proportions. This pose exists because the shipped humanoid rig template is itself an A-pose, so a mesh built from this one is fitted by rigging.fit_template directly instead of needing joints measured off its vertices. It trades some limb separation for that, which is the one thing a single-view reconstruction most needs, and is why the T-pose remains on offer rather than being replaced. This is DATA: the pose is iterable without touching any code.
